english.html: verification and recognition of the said prisoner, calling himself Martin Guerre, as upon the life and repute of the witnesses confronted. The monitory letter published, the revelations re-taken [resumees: the depositions made under the monitoire, repeated before the judge], the inquiries on the court's own motion made, there results, among other things, that the said de Rols has all the time of her life, and even during the absence of the said Martin her husband, lived virtuously and honourably.

english.html: This proof and circumstance was of no small weight [unclear: the print has n'eſtoit pas de poids, "was not of weight"; the sense requires the contrary, and a word seems to have dropped] for the excuse of the said de Rols, and to show that she understood nothing of the fraud: for, besides that nature and the law presume of every man that he is good, honest and of good life a, and that he would not think any fraud or wickedness against his neighbour b, the good opinion is further much increased when by the past it appears of a person that he has always lived as a man of worth, and is, toward all who know him, esteemed and reputed as such c.

NO KEY LETTER IS PRINTED on this second margin block (5 lines 'c. l. non omnes' … 'præſum'), so it is recorded as one note with key null per §4. The x-height glyph + period opening its first line, and the one opening 'c. mandata de', are the abbreviation 'c.' (same size and shape as the 'c.' of 'c. dudũ' in note a; the italic b of 'barbaris' below is a full-ascender letter; the page's one printed key 'a' has no period), not the key letters b and c. Body markers {b} (blocks[2].lines[5]) and {c} (blocks[2].lines[8]) therefore have no keyed note; this unkeyed block serves {b} and/or {c}: 'l. non omnes, P. à barbaris, D. de re milit.' is one Digest citation and 'c. mandata de præſum.' a decretal citation, so it may be two citations run together (b then c) or one for c alone. Placement: its first line stands level with the 'TEXTE.' heading, half a line above 'Et quant au Preuenu, il y a enuiron' (the beside_line given), two body lines below marker c and six below marker b.

At 8x (body-4.jpg, fifth line, x 1170-1290) the top of the stem before the apostrophe curls to the RIGHT into a hook, exactly like the ſ of 'ſon' on the same line (x 110-230), and carries no wedge serif to the left; every l on the line ('la' at x 540-660, 'l'' elsewhere) has the flat wedge serif projecting left at the top. The foot is a two-sided serif, broader than the ſ of 'ſon', but the foot varies between ſ sorts in this face and the top is decisive. Read 'ſ'augmente'.

readings.reason: At 4x (margin-2.jpg, lines 1, 9 and 12 of the margin column, x 90-540) the glyph opening 'c. l. non omnes' and the glyph opening 'c. mandata de' are x-height crescents each followed by a period, identical in size and shape to the 'c.' of 'c. dudũ' on note a's first line; the italic b of 'barbaris' directly below is a full-ascender letter. The column has no hanging key position (note a's key 'a' stands at the same left edge as every other line), and the only printed key on the page, 'a', carries no period. So both glyphs are the abbreviation 'c.' (capitulum), not key letters, and the block has no printed key. Per the coordinator's rule it is kept as ONE unkeyed note serving markers {b} and/or {c}; the grouping into two notes rested only on the supposed keys.
Word division normalized per the standing ruling: 'de re militari' is three distinct words and the tightness of the setting is not the reader's concern; 'remilit.' is not a contraction of the period.
